text: I, MARK HUMBERT, hereby declare that I am a candidate for an elective office in the City of Berkeley, and make the following statement:
1. That my name is Mark Humbert
2. The office for which I am a candidate is Berkeley City Council District 8
3. That my residence is 2928 Linden Avenue, Berkeley, CA 94705
4. The place of my birth is Houston, TX
5. My present occupation is City Councilmember

6. I have held the following public offices: Berkeley City Councilmember, District 8; Commissioner: Berkeley Transportation Commission, Berkeley Public Works Commission, Berkeley Fair Campaign Practices Commission, Berkeley Open Government Commission, Berkeley Parks, Recreation & Waterfront Commission.

7. Record of community service: StopWaste Board Member; Former President, Claremont Elmwood Neighborhood Association; Member, AIDS Legal Referral Panel; Pro Bono Mediator, US District Court, Northern District of California.
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley.

9. It has been a privilege and a pleasure to serve as the District 8 Councilmember for these past four years, and I remain committed to putting essential public services and infrastructure first. In my first term, we’ve enhanced District 8 parks and replaced the Willard Clubhouse with a new, award-winning facility; supported our first responders with superb police and fire chiefs, new technology, and better wildfire preparedness; began investing in smoother, safer streets; updated our zoning laws to enable middle-density homes; and supported community events like the Elmwood Music Festival, Russell Street Halloween, Berkeley Sun Day, and more. There’s still much to be done, so I’m asking for your vote to continue working with you to improve public safety, support our small businesses, fix our streets and sidewalks, and make our city more inclusive and affordable. My pragmatic and collaborative approach is why my colleagues want to work with me for another 4 years. I’m proud to have the endorsements of State Senator Jesse Arreguín, Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, Mayor of Berkeley Adena Ishii and a supermajority of the Berkeley City Council, Berkeley Firefighters Association Local 1227, the Sierra Club, Berkeley School Board Director Jennifer Shanoski, AC Transit Director Jean Walsh, BART Board Director Barnali Ghosh, Peralta Community College Trustee Dyana Delfin-Polk, and more. Join us: www.HumbertForCouncil.com

text: I, MICHAEL WALLMAN, hereby declare that I am a candidate for an elective office in the City of Berkeley, and make the following statement:
1. That my name is Michael Wallman
2. The office for which I am a candidate is City Council District 8
3. That my residence is 59 Arden Rd, Berkeley CA 94704
4. The place of my birth is Oakland, CA
5. My present occupation is Systems Engineer
6. I have held the following public offices: n/a
7. Record of community service: Panoramic Hill Association Board Member; PTA John Muir Elementary Member
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley.

9. Having grown up, raising kids, and caring for elderly family members here in Berkeley, I’ve watched our city change over decades. While shifts occur gradually, the cumulative stress on our community is clear. As an engineer, I analyze data to make sound policy decisions rather than serving special interests or selling out our city to large corporations. I am committed to clean, safe streets, supporting public education, and preserving our parks and open spaces for families across all generations. Living in a Zone Zero neighborhood, fire and earthquake safety are urgent priorities; I will foster close collaboration between the city, fire department, and residents so we can survive a major disaster together. Additionally, development must be balanced—protecting small businesses while accounting for traffic and infrastructure. In the university area, housing policy must protect our neighborhoods and student residents from exploitation while ensuring quality of life. Finally, we must proactively engage the University of California, Berkeley to ensure this large entity respects the integrity, value, and character of our city. Join our cause at wallmandistrict8.com.
10. I refer to the following residents of the City of Berkeley: None

text: I, FRED M FELLER, hereby declare that I am a candidate for an elective office in the City of Berkeley, and make the following statement:
1. That my name is Fred M Feller
2. The office for which I am a candidate is City Council, District 8
3. That my residence is 2819 Benvenue Avenue, Berkeley, CA 94705
4. The place of my birth is Washington D. C.
5. My present occupation is Attorney
6. I have held the following public offices: Commissioner, Berkeley Housing Advisory Commission; Commissioner, Berkeley Police Review Commission

7. Record of community service: Former: Director, Berkeley Public Library Foundation; President, Association of Legal Assistance Workers; President, Berkeley Democratic Club; President, Berkeley Bar Association
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley

9. District 8 deserves an accountable and accessible council representative who listens to residents and small businesses; supports appropriate scale inclusionary housing; fights for public safety initiatives that won’t threaten our privacy; and understands that the vibrant Elmwood commercial district faces many challenges. Throughout the many years I have lived and worked in Berkeley I have devoted my time and energy to community service and civic engagement. I have served as a volunteer and board member for many community organizations, including Berkeley Public Library Foundation, Jewish Family and Community Services and Bay Area Legal Aid. My priorities are to find better ways to build affordable housing in our high resource neighborhoods so that Berkeley can preserve the diversity which makes our community such a wonderful place to live. I have a strong interest in reforming our mental health system and housing the homeless. I want Berkeley to be a city that everyone looks to as a model for the best that a society can provide. For more information on my campaign, please go to my website, www.fredfellerforcouncil.com. I look forward to working with you.

text: I, MARI MENDONCA, hereby declare that I am a candidate for an elective office in the City of Berkeley, and make the following statement:
1. That my name is Mari Mendonca
2. The office for which I am a candidate is Berkeley City Council District 8
3. That my residence is 2166 Ashby Ave Berkeley CA 94705
4. The place of my birth is Berkeley, CA
5. My present occupation is Organizer/Advocate

6. I have held the following public offices: Rent Stabilization Board Commissioner, 4x4 Joint Task Force Committee on Housing, Eviction/Section 8/Foreclosure Committee, Outreach Committee, Community Advisory Group for BART Development.

7. Record of community service: Member of Friends of Adeline, Family Advocate Brave Families Rising Above, Advocate for Harriet Tubman Terrace Tenant Council, Former Steering Committee Member Berkeley Tenants Union
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley.

9. I’m running for City Council District 8 bringing accountable leadership that listens to and respects the needs of Elmwood. I’ll fight hard to preserve it with growth that’s responsible and honors its legacy, which I understand because I’m part of it. I attended Willard Junior High and worked my first job at Colby Pharmacy, a small family business representing its core. I have over 15 years of experience navigating the difficulties of complex issues, including as an elected leader, a Unite Here 2850 union leader, Housing Commission vice-chair and organizer in the Friends of Adeline. Powerful lobbies are influencing leadership to up-zone and infill neighborhoods under the pretense of addressing our so-called housing crisis, including legislation benefitting investors with density bonuses. This doesn’t capture the affordable housing we need and is locally threatening the viability of our small businesses and neighborhood infrastructure, using oversimplified narratives that more is better. It’s not if it’s irresponsible and destructive. What’s required is mindful and responsible leadership who listens and ensures housing, safety, infrastructure, access and accessibility. We can’t afford politics as usual. People have the power. Let’s use ours to vote for accountable leadership and needed change. Vote Mari Nov 3. Electmarimendonca.com
